title: F5 releases out-of-band patches for critical NGINX vulnerabilities
description: F5 has released out-of-band patches for multiple critical vulnerabilities in the NGINX web server, including three critical flaws in the ngx_http_v3_module and the map directive. These vulnerabilities allow remote attackers without privileges to cause denial-of-service or potentially execute code on affected systems with certain configurations. Exploitation involves heap-based buffer overflow or use-after-free conditions, leading to crashes or restarts, and code execution is possible if ASLR is disabled or bypassed. Patches cover various F5 NGINX products such as NGINX Plus, Open Source, Ingress Controller, Gateway Fabric, and Instance Manager. Mitigations are available for those unable to patch immediately. No active exploitation has been reported yet.
aiSummary: F5 addressed three critical vulnerabilities in NGINX components: CVE-2026-15176 and CVE-2026-97205 in the ngx_http_v3_module, and CVE-2026-93479 in the map directive. These flaws enable remote attackers to trigger heap-based buffer overflows or use-after-free bugs in the NGINX worker process, causing denial-of-service or potential remote code execution on systems with non-default configurations and ASLR disabled or bypassed. F5 released out-of-band patches for multiple NGINX products including NGINX Plus, Open Source, Ingress Controller, Gateway Fabric, and Instance Manager. Mitigations include avoiding the 'alias' directive or $request_filename variable, disabling asynchronous file I/O or Server Side Includes, and using named captures in regex blocks. While no exploitation in the wild has been observed, F5 products have historically been targeted by cybercrime and nation-state actors.
aiImpact: Successful exploitation can cause denial-of-service via crashes or restarts of the NGINX worker process due to heap-based buffer overflow or use-after-free vulnerabilities. Additionally, remote code execution is possible on systems where ASLR is disabled or can be bypassed, potentially allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code without privileges. This affects multiple F5 NGINX products and could lead to system compromise or service disruption.
